clue.text: Book lone singer's act on Monday

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the Monday piece follows the rest

parts.note: a lone singer performs a solo, and the act is a song of solo

explanation.surface: A Bible book is pictured as a soloist's Monday performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the Monday piece comes after the singer's act.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Solomon is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Difficult old boys can eat terribly

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, so two of them are OBS
a can is a tin

indicators.note: terribly signals the three letters of eat are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Former pupils who eat tinned food messily make a hard crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult, stubborn person refuses to give way, which is what obstinate describes.

clue.text: Birds, say, about to look up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole thing is read from bottom to top
about means going around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: say, as in for example, is EG
to look is to see

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look up at some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: EG placed about SEE gives ESEEG; 'up' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterfowl, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Having broken rib feel feverish

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of rib and feel are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone with a cracked rib starts to feel hot and unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile is the medical adjective for having a fever.

clue.text: Familiar fellow getting bad cold by chance

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of cold are muddled up

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck

explanation.surface: A friendly man happens to come down with a nasty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges COLD to OLDC. 'Hap' survives in 'haphazard' and 'happen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old chap is an affectionate British form of address for a man one knows well.

clue.text: Try to go too far past a stretch of river

parts.note: past, as in beyond, is over
a reach is a straight stretch of a river

explanation.surface: Someone is pressing on past a section of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to attempt more than one can manage.

clue.text: Perform better than defeated party

parts.note: a batsman or contestant defeated is out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: The losing side is compared with a party that does better.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass or beat someone.

clue.text: Putting on side and arrogance is gross

indicators.note: putting on means faking, so the letters of side and arrogance are made into a false arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone putting on airs and acting arrogantly is called vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on' rearranges SIDE plus ARROGANCE; 'side' also hints at the British sense of pretentiousness, which is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse-grained can mean crude or unrefined, as gross does.

clue.text: Collect for collect in this?

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer, and to collect is to gather, so the clue describes a gathering where people say prayers

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the word collect used twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Collect' is the church noun (a set prayer), the second the verb to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people held for communal praying fits both senses of collect.

clue.text: Place for the rest of the natives?

definitions.text: Place for the rest of the natives?

parts.words: Place for the rest of the natives?
parts.note: natives is a name for oysters raised in British waters, so the clue asks where these shellfish lie at rest

explanation.surface: It sounds like a spot where local people take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natives' are farmed British oysters, such as those from Whitstable, not local people.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabed area where oysters grow or are farmed is where these natives lie.

clue.text: Get in chips with no fish

indicators.note: with no says one piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter, from wood chips
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone orders chips but no fish at the chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips and fish' suggests a British fish supper, but Chips is a ship's carpenter; 'with no' removes CARP.
explanation.definitionFit: To get in somewhere is to come into it, a synonym.

clue.text: Artist is going to Spain, needing lift

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A painter heading for Spain needs a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it, a synonym.

clue.text: Showing agreement in mischief about yen

parts.note: mischief can mean harm or damage
about, as in concerning, is on
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: Getting up to mischief about a longing, yet somehow agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in harmony is to be in accord, sharing agreement.

clue.text: An illustration from old flame -enough

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
ample means enough or plenty

explanation.surface: Someone's former lover is held up as an instance, and that is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is an instance used to illustrate a point.

clue.text: It's of interest, principally, to favoured borrowers

definitions.text: It's of interest, principally, to favoured borrowers

parts.words: It's of interest, principally, to favoured borrowers
parts.note: interest here is the charge on a loan, and principally hints at the first-class rate a bank gives its best customers

explanation.surface: Something that chiefly matters to privileged people who borrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like curiosity but is the banking charge; 'principally' plays on first-rank, the sense of prime.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate banks charge their most creditworthy customers is the lowest lending rate on offer.

clue.text: Diver's headlong fall reported

indicators.note: reported means the word is said rather than written, so we want its sound-alike

parts.note: a purler is British slang for a heavy headlong fall

explanation.surface: A diver's spectacular tumble is described in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech without a sounded R, PURLER and PEARLER sound the same. A pearler dives for pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl diver goes underwater to gather oysters for their pearls.

clue.text: State of a liaison you finally arranged

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters are set out in a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A love affair is set up in some American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives U from 'you'; 'arranged' rearranges A LIAISON plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a US state on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Using thatching to make architectural feature

definitions.meaning: thatch is often made of reeds
a moulding of parallel convex ridges, like bundled reeds, on a column or edge

explanation.surface: A thatcher's work becomes part of a building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from reeds: laying them as thatch, and a moulding carved to look like them.

clue.text: Split over crude results in conflict

parts.note: a gulf is a wide gap or split

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, means the word is flipped and read upwards

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: A row over crude oil leads to fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf War of 1990-91 was the conflict that followed Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

clue.text: Popular place to live is not contracted out

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a house is somewhere to live

explanation.surface: A fashionable home is described as staying within the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done in-house is done by a firm's own staff rather than by outsiders.

clue.text: Receive bequest from popular woman with it

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone gets a legacy from a fashionable lady with sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property left in a will.

clue.text: I shall cure most of the suffering from this?

parts.note: I shall can be shortened to I'll
to cure is to heal

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone vows to cure most of the suffering from a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL plus HEAL plus TH ('most of the', losing its last letter) spells the answer, as if the clue's first words were a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor health is the state people suffer from when they are unwell.

clue.text: Formerly unknown rubbery liquid

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious elastic fluid from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky fluid from rubber trees, used to make rubber.

clue.text: Benefit as laid down

parts.note: to set something is to lay it down

explanation.surface: An advantage is described as fixed in rules.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, an advantage.

clue.text: Tree supplying some special derivative

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tree yields a particular by-product.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'supplying', which is the link joining the tree to the hidden letters, so the definition is just 'Tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing near water.

clue.text: More old paintings returned

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: More old pictures come back from a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than usual.

clue.text: Win reward easily having produced stuff for piano?

indicators.note: easily suggests a relaxed, loose arrangement of the letters of win and reward

explanation.surface: A pianist wins a prize without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily' rearranges WIN plus REWARD. Metal drawn out into fine strands supplies a piano's strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Wire-drawn metal has been pulled into filament, the stuff a piano's strings are made of.

clue.text: Old army type in foreign parts

parts.note: ex means former or old
a Territorial is a member of Britain's Territorial Army of volunteer reservists

explanation.surface: A former reservist soldier is now serving abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterritorial means outside a country's jurisdiction, as abroad.
